newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Visco presents maxi-amendment to budget.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Visco presents maxi-amendment to budget.

text.p: Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco on Monday presented a maxi-amendment to the government's 1997 budget, grouping together a dozen articles concerning fiscal matters into a single clause.

The move, which has yet to be approved by the lower house of parliament's budget commission, could open the way for an eventual confidence motion in Visco's contested plans to reform Italy's creaking fiscal system.

The centre-left government is facing stiff opposition to its budget plans and by fusing together various atricles it would allow confidence motions to swiftly steam roller large chunks of the budget through parliament.
The budget commission is due to finish its work on the budget later on Monday with the whole package going before the full lower house of parliament on Wednesday.
Deputies have until November 17 to vote on the budget after which it goes to the Senate for ratification.

The budget commission is not expected to have time to consider all the amendments that have been put before it, but parliamentarians will be allowed to re-present amendments to the full chamber. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
